sources.origin: Tesla Q2 2026 production, deliveries and deployments

claims.claim: Q2 vehicle deliveries materially above production are a favorable inventory-conversion signal but cannot be extrapolated as same-quarter manufacturing growth; demand, incentives and inventory timing remain separate mechanisms.

Company-compiled delivery consensus is useful expectation context but is not company guidance, and vehicle outperformance should not be generalized to storage where execution was closer to expectations.

risks: inventory/timing effects can inflate interpretation of one-quarter deliveries
vehicle and storage margins/capital intensity differ
issuer-compiled consensus can create confidence inflation if treated as guidance
competitive substitution across EV and storage markets
contradictions: Deliveries beating expectations is real execution evidence, while deliveries exceeding production means part of the quarter's strength came from inventory conversion; both must remain explicit.
improvementPaths: reconcile deliveries, production, inventory and automotive margin over subsequent quarters
separately evidence storage economics rather than aggregating physical deployment growth

recommendation.reason: Beta challenge is complete; existing delivery-versus-production and cross-vector contradictions need disposition with financial evidence, not automatic blocking.
